subject: Jaguar
fact: Jaguars have powerful jaws and often live near rivers in tropical forests.

subject: Ocelot
fact: Ocelots are spotted wild cats that are active mostly at night.

subject: Margay
fact: Margays can rotate their ankles to climb down tree trunks headfirst.

subject: Harpy Eagle
fact: Harpy eagles have huge talons and hunt high in rainforest canopies.

subject: Toucan
fact: Toucans use their large colorful bills to reach fruit on branches.

subject: Scarlet Macaw
fact: Scarlet macaws use strong curved beaks to crack nuts and seeds.

subject: Howler Monkey
fact: Howler monkeys make very loud calls that can travel through the forest.

subject: Spider Monkey
fact: Spider monkeys use long arms and tails to swing between branches.

subject: Capuchin Monkey
fact: Capuchin monkeys are clever and use their hands to explore food and objects.

subject: Sloth
fact: Sloths move slowly and spend much of their lives hanging in trees.

subject: Giant Anteater
fact: Giant anteaters use long sticky tongues to eat ants and termites.

subject: Tapir
fact: Tapirs have short flexible snouts that help them grab leaves and fruit.

subject: Capybara
fact: Capybaras are the largest living rodents and are excellent swimmers.

subject: Coati
fact: Coatis use long noses to sniff for insects, fruit, and other food.

subject: Kinkajou
fact: Kinkajous have prehensile tails that help them grip branches.

subject: Agouti
fact: Agoutis bury seeds and can help new rainforest plants grow.

subject: Peccary
fact: Peccaries are pig-like mammals that often travel in groups.

subject: Giant Otter
fact: Giant otters live in South American rivers and hunt together in family groups.

subject: Green Anaconda
fact: Green anacondas are heavy snakes that spend lots of time in and near water.

subject: Boa Constrictor
fact: Boa constrictors squeeze prey with their strong muscular bodies.

subject: Emerald Tree Boa
fact: Emerald tree boas coil around branches while resting in trees.

subject: Green Iguana
fact: Green iguanas are strong climbers and mostly eat leaves and fruit.

subject: Basilisk Lizard
fact: Basilisk lizards can run across the surface of water for short distances.

subject: Caiman
fact: Caimans are crocodilian reptiles that live in rivers, lakes, and wetlands.

subject: Poison Dart Frog
fact: Many poison dart frogs have bright colors that warn predators to stay away.

subject: Red-Eyed Tree Frog
fact: Red-eyed tree frogs have sticky toe pads that help them climb leaves.

subject: Glass Frog
fact: Some glass frogs have partly transparent skin on their undersides.

subject: Golden Poison Frog
fact: Golden poison frogs are tiny rainforest frogs with very bright warning colors.

subject: Leafcutter Ant
fact: Leafcutter ants carry leaf pieces to underground gardens where they grow fungus for food.

subject: Army Ant
fact: Army ants travel in large groups while searching the forest floor for food.

subject: Blue Morpho Butterfly
fact: Blue morpho butterflies flash bright blue when their wings catch the light.

subject: Owl Butterfly
fact: Owl butterflies have large eye-like spots on their wings.

subject: Atlas Moth
fact: Atlas moths are among the largest moths in the world by wing area.

subject: Orchid Mantis
fact: Orchid mantises use flower-like shapes and colors to blend into plants.

subject: Goliath Beetle
fact: Goliath beetles are among the heaviest insects in the world.

subject: Rhinoceros Beetle
fact: Male rhinoceros beetles have horn-like structures used in contests with other males.

subject: Walking Stick
fact: Walking sticks resemble twigs, helping them hide from predators.

subject: Leaf Insect
fact: Leaf insects have bodies shaped and colored like leaves.

subject: Tarantula
fact: Tarantulas are large spiders that use venom to subdue small prey.

subject: Golden Silk Orb-Weaver
fact: Golden silk orb-weavers spin strong webs with silk that can look golden in sunlight.

subject: Toucanet
fact: Toucanets are smaller relatives of toucans with bright bills and feathers.

subject: Hoatzin
fact: Young hoatzins have small claws on their wings that can help them climb.

subject: Hornbill
fact: Hornbills often have large curved bills and many species nest in tree cavities.

subject: King Vulture
fact: King vultures help clean forests by eating dead animals.

subject: Quetzal
fact: Resplendent quetzals eat fruit and help spread seeds through cloud forests.

subject: Cassowary
fact: Cassowaries are large flightless birds that help spread rainforest seeds.

subject: Bird-of-Paradise
fact: Many birds-of-paradise have colorful feathers used in courtship displays.

subject: Sun Bear
fact: Sun bears use long tongues to reach honey and insects.

subject: Binturong
fact: Binturongs are tree-dwelling mammals with tails that can grip branches.

subject: Malayan Tapir
fact: Malayan tapirs have bold black-and-white coloring as adults.

subject: Orangutan
fact: Orangutans build leafy sleeping nests high in trees.

subject: Proboscis Monkey
fact: Male proboscis monkeys are known for their large noses.

subject: Gibbon
fact: Gibbons swing through trees using very long arms.

subject: Clouded Leopard
fact: Clouded leopards have large canine teeth and are excellent climbers.

subject: Sumatran Tiger
fact: Sumatran tigers are the smallest living tiger subspecies.

subject: Asian Elephant
fact: Asian elephants use their trunks to breathe, smell, drink, and grasp objects.

subject: Pygmy Hippo
fact: Pygmy hippos are smaller than common hippos and live near West African forests.

subject: Okapi
fact: Okapis have striped legs and are close relatives of giraffes.

subject: Western Lowland Gorilla
fact: Western lowland gorillas eat fruit, leaves, stems, and other plants.

subject: Mandrill
fact: Mandrills are large monkeys with colorful faces and strong canine teeth.
